text: Hello and welcome to our live text commentary of this Premier League match between Fulham and Brentford at Craven Cottage.
Fulham got their Premier League season off to a good start with their 1-0 win away to Everton on the opening matchday.
However, the Cottagers have never won both of their opening two games in any of their 28 previous seasons as a top-flight side.
A West London derby against neighbours Brentford will be a tough game in which to buck that trend.
As ever, Brentford look a tough team to beat: their 2-2 draw with Tottenham last time out was their 15th Premier League draw since the start of last season, more than any other side.
The Bees look more than capable of coping without their suspended star man Ivan Toney.
Let's see how they fare here!
Marco Silva makes two changes to Fulham from their win over Everton.
Pereira comes into midfield.
De Cordova-Reid replaces Willian in their front three.
Brentford make just one change from their draw with Spurs as they switch to a back four.
Schade replaces Ajer in the starting lineup.
This will be a tricky game for Fulham.
The hosts have won just one of their last seven games against Brentford, although it was a 3-2 victory in this exact figure last season.
The Bees are unbeaten in their last 10 Premier League London derbies and have lost just two of their last 16 away league games at Craven Cottage.
Fulham get this game underway! It's a bright, sunny day at Craven Cottage.
Brentford start the game positively, turning a long throw-in down their left into a free-kick as Wilson catches Jensen.
Frank's men are renowned for their set-piece prowess.
The ball's whipped towards the penalty spot.
It's flicked on to Wissa who blasts way off target from the right of the box.
Fulham goal-kick.
Flekken takes too much time on the ball and Jimenez nips in to intercept.
Henry is forced to come across to hand Fulham a corner.
Pereira's excellent corner lands in the centre of the box.
Diop can't keep his effort down.
Lukic gets a free-kick in his own half as he's stopped by Norgaard.
Fulham are enjoying much of the early possession.
Pereira goes for goal from a considerable distance as Brentford sit deep.
It's an ambitious effort that flies high over the crossbar.
Fulham pass the ball from side to side, trying to find a chink in Brentford's armour.
It's proving difficult so far.
Schade knocks the ball inside but can't get to it ahead of Tete without fouling the Dutchman.
Robinson switches off briefly, allowing Mbeumo to sneak in behind him and latch onto Jensen's throughball.
Leno comfortably saves Mbeumo's shot to spare his team-mate's blushes.
Brentford are conserving energy at the moment, sitting back and soaking up pressure from Fulham.
It's working so far.
Jensen takes a free-kick quickly from deep, almost catching Leno off-guard.
Fulham's goalkeeper scrambles back and is relieved to watch the shot bounce comfortably wide.
Jimenez is caught offside from Diop's direct ball from the back.
Silva shouts some words of encouragement to his players.
Henry arrives late on Wilson, handing Fulham a free-kick down their right.
Pereira fires it in, Schade fluffs a header, and Pinnock blocks Diop's hopeful shot.
Flekken rushes off his line to push Pereira's dangerous cross out for a corner.
The Brentford keeper stays alert to clear the ball in as it comes too close to his near post.
Brentford go up the other end of the pitch and get a free-kick down their right.
Jensen swings a cross into the box.
Norgaard's header is close to testing Leno but misses to the right.
Wissa gets a routine save out of the keeper.
Brentford are starting to venture forward more now.
The visitors have been the more convincing side so far.
Henry strays just offside as he races towards Schade's throughball.
Brentford regain possession quickly, and Wissa shoots low from outside the box.
It's straight at Leno, but a warning sign for Fulham.
Jensen's cross from the left is easily caught by Leno.
Brentford can be content with how they've played in this opening half hour.
Jimenez earns Fulham a corner down their left.
Pereira puts spin on the delivery and Pinnock's nudged in the back by Tete, heading against his own crossbar at the near post! The referee blows for a Brentford free-kick.
Fulham are still trying to press the issue, but they're having limited success.
They need more variety in their play.
De Cordova-Reid shoots from outside the box.
It's blocked.
Robinson's powerful cross from the left gets headed away.
There's no room for Fulham through the middle at all.
Tete goes on a mazy run towards the penalty area, eventually being stopped by the Brentford defence.
The Dutchman shouts in frustration as Jensen buys a free-kick.
Big chance for Brentford! Mbeumo slips into the left of the box after a corner and crosses towards the centre.
Wissa connects with the ball but can only scuff his effort wide.
Robinson hastily puts it out for a corner.
Pereira gets another chance to trouble Brentford from a set piece.
This time his delivery is low and flat.
Collins clears.
Hickey's shown the game's first yellow card for a scything tackle on Lukic.
Mbeumo receives the ball on the right wing.
He checks onto his left foot and dinks it into the centre.
Leno catches it.
Jensen twirls through midfield to lay off to Mbeumo outside the box.
Fulham close down the Cameroon international's resulting shot.
GOAL! FULHAM 0-1 BRENTFORD! Wissa capitalises on a foolish mistake from Fulham! Diop mishits a backpass to Leno, allowing the DR Congo forward to nip in, round the keeper and slot into the empty net.
There will be just two added minutes before we take a break for half-time.
Fulham need to regroup at half-time.
They haven't won in their last 12 Premier League matches when conceding the opening goal, dating back to October 2022 against Leeds United.
Ream picks up a booking just before the break for a late challenge on Wissa.
That'll be all for now.
HALF-TIME: FULHAM 0-1 BRENTFORD
Wissa's goal on the stroke of half-time is the difference in this West London derby so far.
Brentford have executed their game plan perfectly, holding Fulham at arm's length and waiting for them to make a mistake.
Diop made it.
Now the hosts have work to do.
More to come!
A few great set pieces from Pereira aside, Flekken's had an easy time in Brentford's goal so far.
Fulham haven't had a shot on target yet.
They'll need to trouble the Dutchman more in the second half if they want to get anything out of this game.
Brentford get the second half started.
Neither side has made any changes.
Jensen hurls a long throw-in into Fulham's box from the left.
Collins gets his head to it but can't divert it on target.
Brentford's goalscorer Wissa gets clattered by three Fulham players on the edge of his own box.
The Bees get a free-kick.
Schade, who's switched to the left for Brentford since the start of the game, tussles with Tete but the Dutchman stands his ground.
Pinnock makes a strong block to deny Jimenez's shot from outside the box and concede a corner.
It doesn't beat the first man in Norgaard.
De Cordova-Reid hits the woodwork! Some good movement down Fulham's right allows the forward to reach Reed's lay-off in the box and curl a first-time shot against the crossbar.
That's the closest that Fulham have come to scoring.
Now Brentford almost double their lead! Leno makes an excellent stop to deny Jensen.
Frank's men get a corner which Fulham defend admirably.
Fulham survive another Brentford throw-in from the right and spring forward on the counter.
Collins reads Jimenez's cute ball inside and intercepts it with ease.
Wilson sends Pereira scampering down the right.
The Brazilian twists this way and that, eventually hanging the ball up for an easy catch by Flekken.
Wilson has plenty of time and space to pick a shot from outside the box.
The one he picks bounces straight into the arms of Flekken.
There's a hint of a penalty for Fulham as Pereira tussles with Norgaard and goes down just inside the box.
The referee Darren Bond isn't persuaded.
Henry's shown the yellow card for time wasting.
That's part of the new directive referees have been given.
PENALTY FOR BRENTFORD! Brentford earn a corner down their right when Wissa's shot from close range gets blocked.
The visitors keep the pressure on and Ream bundles over the forward when the ball comes back in the box.
The referee points straight to the spot!
Reed's booked for protesting the penalty decision.
It's arguably soft, but it is correct.
RED CARD FOR FULHAM! Things go from bad to worse for Fulham.
Ream's foul was his second bookable offence of the game, so he has to go! This game is slipping away from the hosts.
GOAL! FULHAM 0-2 BRENTFORD! Mbeumo takes a short run-up and cheekily dispatches the penalty into the bottom left corner, leaving Leno rooted to the spot.
The three points look to be going the Bees' way.
Reed's the next Fulham player to be sacrificed.
On comes their Nigerian centre-back Bassey.
De Cordova-Reid's the last man to go.
Palhinha enters the fray for Fulham.
Fulham react to their parlous situation by making a triple substitution.
Pereira's first to go off.
Willian replaces him.
Fulham get a corner out of Henry.
Brentford, who've looked solid all game, block Jimenez's shot from the left of the box.
Brentford make their first substitution of the game.
Lewis-Potter replaces the slippery Schade.
Wissa's caught offside from Jensen's throughball.
The momentum Fulham had been building since half-time has understandably vanished since Brentford's second goal.
It's a Brentford corner.
The Bees swarm the box and Pinnock nods Jensen's delivery wide.
Wissa fouls Leno to hand Fulham a brief reprieve.
Brentford are seeing more of the ball now Fulham are down to 10 men.
This is becoming a stroll in the park for them.
Now it's Brentford's turn to make a triple substitution.
Roerslev replaces Hickey first.
Norgaard's next to make way.
On comes his compatriot Damsgaard for Brentford.
Wissa, who opened the scoring for Brentford, gets an early rest.
Dasilva comes on in his place.
Wilson comes inside off the flank and gets nudged over by Jensen just outside the box.
Fulham prepare to take the free-kick...
Willian's free-kick is a touch too high to trouble Flekken, dipping over the crossbar.
That's when Fulham needed Pereira on the pitch.
There's no suggestion that Fulham are going to score here.
The hosts huff and puff, firing a few manageable crosses into Brentford's box.
Flekken eventually pumps clear.
Palhinha kicks the ball away after snapping into a tackle.
He becomes the latest Fulham player to get booked.
Fulham make more changes.
They feel in vain now.
Muniz replaces Tete.
Jimenez, who's been quiet, goes off.
On comes his former Wolves team-mate Traore for Fulham.
This looks bad for Dasilva.
The Brentford substitute slips and appears to injure his hamstring.
It doesn't seem that bad an injury, but he won't be able to carry on sadly.
Dasilva trudges off the pitch escorted by a physio.
Ajer takes his place for the last few minutes.
There will be nine minutes of added time.
Brentford are heading for an easy victory.
GOAL! FULHAM 0-3 BRENTFORD! Mbeumo grabs his second goal of the game, converting Ajer's cross from the byline with a simple tap-in.
It's been a great showing by Brentford.
Usually a centre-back, Ajer strode forward from right-back, drew Leno off his line and put the ball on a plate for Mbeumo.
There was nothing Fulham could do.
Lewis-Potter is unceremoniously clipped by Diop, who's lucky to avoid a booking.
The Fulham centre-back's had a miserable game.
From the free-kick, Ajer's shot from the centre of the box is blocked.
Lewis-Potter has a go himself, and manages to a simple save out of Leno.
Wilson reaches Lukic's througball to shoot at Flekken from a difficult angle on the right.
The Brentford keeper has it covered.
There's a brief stop in play when Wilson picks up a knock to the head.
Thankfully it's minor and he's soon back on his feet.
Henry, now playing on the right, strays offside.
Brentford are steely, versatile, and they've got the win here!
FULL-TIME: FULHAM 0-3 BRENTFORD
Brentford stroll home from this West London Derby with all three points! The Bees had Fulham's number all game, taking the lead just before half-time through Wissa.
The hosts' brief revival came to an end when they went down to 10 men and Mbeumo made it 2-0.
The Cameroon forward struck again late on to seal the win for Frank's men.
Brentford climb to second in the nascent Premier League table.
They're unbeaten in their last five Premier League games and look capable of causing any team in this league problems, with or without Toney.
Fulham sit 10th.
They were outplayed here, but they'll face less street-smart opponents this season.
Brentford have given Fulham an early sting then.
We'll see what bearing it has on both teams' seasons.
That's all for now.
Goodbye!
